title: AI Marketing Statistics Source Ledger
methodology: Markethink curated only claims that were visible in an original report, official dataset, or original survey page that loaded during review. Each row preserves scope, sample context, evidence type, and a limitation. Self-reported outcomes are not causal evidence. Values from unlike questions are not treated as directly comparable.

S1.publisher: U.S. Census Bureau, Center for Economic Studies
S1.title: The Microstructure of AI Diffusion: Evidence from Firms, Business Functions, and Worker Tasks
S1.sample_size: Nationally representative Business Trends and Outlook Survey AI supplement; exact n not stated on the summary page
S1.limitation: Firm adoption, employment-weighted adoption, and worker task use are different measures. The survey does not isolate marketing departments.

S2.title: AI use by individuals surges across the OECD as adoption by firms continues to expand
S2.geography: OECD countries where data were available
S2.sample_size: National business ICT surveys compiled in the OECD ICT Access and Usage Database; n varies by country
S2.limitation: Coverage is limited to countries with available data. Definitions and business-size thresholds can vary by national source.

S3.title: Small Business and Technology 2025
S3.research_period: 2025; exact field dates not stated in the report text
S3.sample_size: 521 employer responses overall; AI-use questions use smaller bases, including n=118, n=119, and n=110
S3.limitation: The sample is drawn from NFIB members, and several AI-use findings apply only to the smaller subset of current users.

S4.title: The Rise of the SMB Creator: Q2 2026 Small Business Now report findings
S4.research_period: Q2 2026; US adoption figure measured by April 2026
S4.geography: United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia and New Zealand
S4.source_type: Original vendor-commissioned SMB and consumer survey
S4.limitation: The publisher sells marketing technology. The release uses a broad SMB marketing AI adoption measure that is not directly comparable with the NFIB business-use question.

S5.title: B2B Content and Marketing Trends: Insights for 2026
S5.limitation: Results are self-reported. The research was sponsored by a marketing technology company, and the B2B sample was mostly North American.

S6.title: Adobe 2026 AI and Digital Trends Report

S6.limitation: Business results are self-reported by executives and CX practitioners at organizations with at least $250 million in revenue. Customer results are a separate sample.

S7.title: The AI Ad Gap Widens
S7.publication_date: 2026; exact day not stated on the report page
S7.sample_size: 505 Gen Z and Millennial consumers plus 104 ad industry executives
